content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi, I need to create a report showing customer names and their total number of orders.
Certainly. Can you confirm the table and column names for customers and orders, especially which field links them?
The tables are 'customers' and 'orders'. Customers has 'id', 'name', and 'email'. Orders has 'id', 'customer_id', and 'order_date'.

Thanks for clarifying. Here is a parameterized SQL query that gives each customer's name and their order count:
```sql
SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.name;
```
Looks good! But can you exclude customers who haven't placed any orders?

Of course. You can add a HAVING clause to filter out customers with zero orders:
```sql
SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.name
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 0;
```
Can you add the customer email to the result as well?

Sure. Here's the updated query, including the email and following compliance best practices:
```sql
SELECT c.name, c.email, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.name, c.email
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 0;
```
I'm using Postgres. Do I need to change anything for this to work?
This query will work in Postgres as written. For extra safety, consider using parameterized queries if you embed this in application code.
How about masking the email domain for privacy, so only the name shows?

Great idea. Here's how to mask the domain in Postgres:
```sql
SELECT c.name, SUBSTRING(c.email FROM 1 FOR POSITION('@' IN c.email)-1) || '@***' AS masked_email, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.name, masked_email
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 0;
```
Can you adapt that for MySQL too?

Certainly! Here's the MySQL version for domain masking:
```sql
SELECT c.name, CONCAT(SUBSTRING_INDEX(c.email, '@', 1), '@***') AS masked_email, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.name, masked_email
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 0;
```
If I want to see only customers with more than 5 orders, what should I change?

Just update the HAVING clause:
```sql
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 5;
```
Thanks! One last thing, can you show me the full query for Snowflake with these requirements?

Absolutely! Here's a Snowflake-compliant query, masking email domains and showing customers with more than 5 orders:
```sql
SELECT c.name, SUBSTR(c.email, 1, POSITION('@' IN c.email)-1) || '@***' AS masked_email, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.name, masked_email
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 5;
```
